subject.title: feat(msteams): Microsoft Teams voice (CVI) + video + chat + governance

question: Should OpenClaw land Microsoft Teams CVI/chat governance as this full bundled integration, split it into staged owner-reviewed PRs, or route the provider/companion-worker integration outside core through a plugin/ClawHub-owned package?
rationale: The branch combines a new voice-call provider, Teams channel governance, public realtime/TTS SDK changes, config/default additions, session routing, and security-sensitive bridge behavior; automation cannot choose the product boundary or acceptable review scope.

options.title: Split And Stage The Landing
options.body: Keep the PR open but require a maintainer-chosen sequence, such as provider/bridge first, then SDK/TTS, chat governance, meeting productivity, and security surfaces with proof per stage.

options.title: Accept The Full Integration
options.body: Maintainers can land this as one exceptional feature branch only after conflict refresh, green required checks, and explicit owner/security/API approval.

options.title: Move To External Plugin Path
options.body: If Teams CVI and the companion worker are not intended as bundled core scope, preserve the proof/API-gap discussion and move the integration to an owner plugin or ClawHub path.

recommendation.title: Split And Stage The Landing
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require a maintainer-chosen sequence, such as provider/bridge first, then SDK/TTS, chat governance, meeting productivity, and security surfaces with proof per stage.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest sampled history across plugin boundaries, voice-call, msteams, and SDK refactors touched by the decision.
